verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents a persistent memory system: it writes plain Markdown files to the agent's workspace so information survives across sessions, and there is a dedicated docs page on 'How OpenClaw remembers things across sessions.' However, the same docs caveat that 'the model only remembers what gets saved to disk,' implying memory capture depends on the agent (or user) explicitly saving notes rather than a fully automatic, transparent long-term memory store, and there's no independent/community corroboration of recall reliability. Missing for 10: evidence of fully automatic (no manual trigger) memory writes, semantic/searchable recall beyond flat files, and hands-on user reports confirming it 'just remembers' reliably.
